title: AR-Matched Bragg Stack with Impedance Grading
scientific_hypothesis: Adding anti-reflection matching layers at the air interface will reduce passband ripple in the 1530-1565 nm transmission band while maintaining visible band reflectance.
design_principle: Impedance mismatch at air-dielectric interface causes passband ripple. L13 demonstrates Al2O3/SiO2 AR coatings; L22 shows quarter-wave AR layers improve transmission bandwidth. SiO2 AR layers can grade the index transition.
proposed_topology: Air | SiO2 (AR) | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | SiO2 (AR) | Fused Silica substrate (9 Bragg pairs + 2 AR layers = 20 layers total)
design_variables: AR layer thicknesses (2 variables), Bragg quarter-wave reference wavelength (1 variable)
manufacturing_considerations: AR layers use same materials as Bragg stack (no additional materials)
SiO2 AR layer on fused silica substrate provides index grading
expected_advantages: Reduced passband ripple compared to unmatched Bragg stack
Better transmission uniformity across 1530-1565 nm band
known_risks: AR layers may reduce visible band reflectance
May not improve overall target score if ripple is not limiting factor
execution_request_english: Design a multilayer dielectric stack with air incidence on fused silica substrate. Stack: SiO2 (Lemarchand) AR layer at air interface, followed by 9 alternating pairs of HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) (starting with HfO2), followed by SiO2 (Lemarchand) AR layer at substrate interface (20 layers total). Optimize the two AR layer thicknesses and the Bragg quarter-wave reference wavelength to maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band while maximizing reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Layer count fixed at 20. Materials: hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand).
